build.reason: The recipe compiles the UTF-8 target against the static library; the legacy salt function remains declared and defined. This is a static compatibility assessment, not a claimed build run.

input.reason: For byte lengths the target passes as an int, it supplies the same buffer and length to both parse calls; the parser accepts that argument form. Its size assertion restricts the invocation to the API's int-length domain.

lifecycle.reason: The target keeps the parent alive while creating and freeing children, resets only after parsing, and frees children before the parent.

control_flow.reason: Creation leads to salt setup, handlers, parsing, optional reset, child creation, and cleanup. The new legacy setter preserves the call; parse errors are handled without an assertion.

accepted.requirement: Exercise the supported pre-parse configuration of a parser with a caller-supplied 16-byte hash salt, including its use by hashing and inheritance by external-entity parsers.
accepted.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates root and namespace parsers, then ParseOneInput calls XML_SetHashSalt with an unsigned-long SipHash result before XML_Parse. The parent subsequently creates external-entity parsers.
accepted.failure_condition: For any ordinary valid XML input, such as <a/>, the target has no call that supplies 16 entropy bytes. Its legacy setter fixes the high key half to zero. Thus no target call sequence exercises a caller-chosen full-width salt.
accepted.alternative_paths: Automatic generation, including the possible zero-legacy-salt route, chooses a library-generated value; it cannot exercise a caller-supplied 16-byte value. The target's other parser calls use the same ParseOneInput helper, and child parsers inherit the parent's configured key.

source_evidence.quote:
/* Added in Expat 2.7.6. */
XML_Bool XMLCALL
XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes(XML_Parser parser,
                       const uint8_t entropy[16]);
Sets the hash salt to use for internal hash calculations. Helps in preventing DoS attacks based on predicting hash function behavior. In order to have an effect this must be called before parsing has started. Returns XML_TRUE if successful, XML_FALSE when called after XML_Parse or XML_ParseBuffer or when parser is NULL.

Note: Setting a salt that is not from a source of high quality entropy (like getentropy(3)) will make the parser vulnerable to hash flooding attacks.

Note: This call is optional, as the parser will auto-generate a new random salt value internally if no value has been set by the start of parsing.
